questions.stem: This labeled diagram shows leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles, with an anterior leaflet and anterior annulus. Which structure normally prevents these leaflets from everting into the atrium during systole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The moderator band bracing the free wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chordae tendineae anchoring the leaflets to the papillary muscles

choices.label: C
choices.text: The trabeculae carneae lining the ventricular apex

choices.label: D
choices.text: The interventricular septum pushing the leaflets shut

choices.label: E
choices.text: The annular ring contracting to seal the orifice

explanation.summary: During systole the papillary muscles contract and the chordae tendineae hold the mitral leaflets in a closed position, preventing them from prolapsing back into the left atrium. Failure of this apparatus (e.g., chordal rupture) leads to regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: During systole the papillary muscles contract and the chordae tendineae hold the mitral leaflets in a closed position, preventing them from prolapsing back into the left atrium. Failure of this apparatus (e.g., chordal rupture) leads to regurgitation.

questions.stem: This cadaveric atrial-view photograph shows a large anterior leaflet, a scalloped posterior leaflet (P1-P3 segments), and anterolateral and posteromedial commissures. Which cardiac valve is displayed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aortic valve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pulmonary valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitral valve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tricuspid valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coronary sinus ostium

explanation.summary: The bileaflet arrangement with a single broad anterior leaflet, a scalloped three-segment posterior leaflet, and two commissures is the hallmark surgical anatomy of the mitral valve viewed from the left atrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bileaflet arrangement with a single broad anterior leaflet, a scalloped three-segment posterior leaflet, and two commissures is the hallmark surgical anatomy of the mitral valve viewed from the left atrium.

questions.stem: This diagram shows a catheter advanced from the inferior vena cava through the right atrium, across a transseptal puncture into the left atrium, with a balloon inflated at the mitral valve. What procedure is being performed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mitral annuloplasty ring placement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement

choices.label: C
choices.text: Radiofrequency pulmonary vein ablation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty

choices.label: E
choices.text: Left atrial appendage occlusion

explanation.summary: A catheter reaches the left atrium via a transseptal puncture, and a balloon is inflated across the stenotic mitral orifice to split the fused commissures. This percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty relieves obstruction in favorable rheumatic mitral stenosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: A catheter reaches the left atrium via a transseptal puncture, and a balloon is inflated across the stenotic mitral orifice to split the fused commissures. This percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty relieves obstruction in favorable rheumatic mitral stenosis.

questions.stem: This illustration traces a clot forming in the heart and lodging in a cerebral artery, with atrial fibrillation labeled at the heart. In a patient with mitral stenosis, what best explains this sequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aortic atherosclerotic plaque ruptures and showers the cerebral arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carotid stenosis alone produces the obstruction, unrelated to the heart

choices.label: C
choices.text: Right-to-left shunting sends venous clots directly into the carotid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endocarditis vegetations embolize from the aortic valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Left atrial stasis and atrial fibrillation promote thrombus that embolizes to the brain, causing stroke

explanation.summary: Mitral stenosis dilates the left atrium and predisposes to atrial fibrillation. Blood stasis in the fibrillating, enlarged atrium fosters thrombus formation; dislodged clot travels through the systemic circulation and can occlude a cerebral artery, producing a cardioembolic stroke.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mitral stenosis dilates the left atrium and predisposes to atrial fibrillation. Blood stasis in the fibrillating, enlarged atrium fosters thrombus formation; dislodged clot travels through the systemic circulation and can occlude a cerebral artery, producing a cardioembolic stroke.

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows a mitral valve viewed from the atrium with a narrowed, slit-like central orifice and thickened, retracted leaflets. What diagnosis does this appearance represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bicuspid aortic valve

choices.label: B
choices.text: A flail leaflet from ruptured chordae

choices.label: C
choices.text: A normal, widely patent mitral valve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacterial vegetations of infective endocarditis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mitral stenosis with a fish-mouth orifice

explanation.summary: Chronic (usually rheumatic) inflammation fuses the commissures and thickens the leaflets, reducing the opening to a narrow fish-mouth slit. This is the classic gross appearance of mitral stenosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic (usually rheumatic) inflammation fuses the commissures and thickens the leaflets, reducing the opening to a narrow fish-mouth slit. This is the classic gross appearance of mitral stenosis.

questions.stem: This gross specimen (panel C) shows a mitral valve with a reduced orifice and an arrow pointing to yellow-tan nodular material along the thickened leaflet. What does the arrowed material most likely represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fresh red thrombus adherent to the leaflet

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fatty streaks of early atheroma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myxomatous ground substance expanding the leaflet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Friable infective vegetations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Calcific deposits within the fibrotic stenotic valve

explanation.summary: Long-standing mitral stenosis leads to fibrosis with dystrophic calcification of the leaflets and commissures. The firm yellow-tan nodular deposits indicated by the arrow are calcium, which stiffens the valve and further narrows the orifice.
explanation.whyCorrect: Long-standing mitral stenosis leads to fibrosis with dystrophic calcification of the leaflets and commissures. The firm yellow-tan nodular deposits indicated by the arrow are calcium, which stiffens the valve and further narrows the orifice.

questions.stem: This diagram compares a normal heart with one showing mitral valve stenosis, where the mitral orifice is narrowed as blood passes from the left atrium to the left ventricle. What is the principal hemodynamic consequence of the narrowing shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impaired diastolic filling of the left ventricle with elevated left atrial pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduced afterload allowing rapid ventricular emptying

choices.label: C
choices.text: Backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle in diastole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Systolic backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased forward stroke volume from the left ventricle

explanation.summary: A narrowed mitral orifice obstructs flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle during diastole. Pressure builds behind the valve, raising left atrial and pulmonary venous pressures while the left ventricle remains underfilled, producing the diastolic rumble and pulmonary congestion of mitral stenosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: A narrowed mitral orifice obstructs flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle during diastole. Pressure builds behind the valve, raising left atrial and pulmonary venous pressures while the left ventricle remains underfilled, producing the diastolic rumble and pulmonary congestion of mitral stenosis.

questions.stem: The left panel shows pressure-volume loops (normal vs mitral stenosis) and the right panel shows pressure tracings where left atrial pressure exceeds left ventricular pressure during diastole. What does this persistent diastolic LA-to-LV pressure difference represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A regurgitant v wave from mitral incompetence

choices.label: B
choices.text: The transmitral diastolic pressure gradient caused by the stenotic valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal ventricular-arterial coupling during ejection

choices.label: D
choices.text: The systolic gradient across a stenotic aortic valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pressure drop across an obstructed pulmonary valve

explanation.summary: A normal open mitral valve allows LA and LV diastolic pressures to equalize. In mitral stenosis the narrowed orifice sustains a pressure gradient, so LA pressure stays above LV pressure throughout diastole. The PV loop also shows the reduced LV filling and smaller stroke volume that result.
explanation.whyCorrect: A normal open mitral valve allows LA and LV diastolic pressures to equalize. In mitral stenosis the narrowed orifice sustains a pressure gradient, so LA pressure stays above LV pressure throughout diastole. The PV loop also shows the reduced LV filling and smaller stroke volume that result.
